operations.name: join
operations.description:
Registers a new user account by creating a record in the todo_app_users table with provided email and hashed password.

This operation creates a new user account when a member user completes the registration workflow. The email field is captured from the request and stored as the primary identifier, while the password_hash field is populated with a bcrypt-hashed value generated from the submitted password. The operation succeeds only if the email is unique in the system and meets character length requirements.

The implementation directly references the todo_app_users table schema, using its email and password_hash fields as defined in the database model. No other fields are manipulated during registration.

After successful creation, the system generates a new JWT access token and refresh token pair. The access token is valid for 15 minutes and embedded in the response, while the refresh token is stored securely and used for subsequent token refresh operations.

This operation provides the foundational authentication flow for member users to gain access to their personal todo lists, which are protected by the user's credential system.

Related operations: /auth/user/login for re-authentication, /auth/user/refresh for token renewal.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user identifier returned after successful registration.

operations.specification: Service layer validates email format and uniqueness against todo_app_users table. Hashes password using bcrypt with cost factor 12. Creates new record with email, password_hash, and empty password_reset_token. Generates JWT access token with 15-minute expiration and refresh token with 7-day expiration. Stores refresh token in secure session store. Returns access token in response header and refresh token in httpOnly cookie.

operations.name: login
operations.description:
Authenticates an existing user by validating email and password_hash against the todo_app_users table.

This endpoint accepts user credentials and verifies them against the stored email and password_hash values in the todo_app_users table. The system checks if a user with the provided email exists and if the submitted password matches the stored password_hash value generated by bcrypt during registration.

The operation references the password_hash field directly from the schema and implements the bcrypt verification algorithm to compare hashes without storing passwords in plaintext. No other schema fields are involved in the authentication process.

On successful authentication, the system generates a new JWT access token (valid for 15 minutes) and refresh token (valid for 7 days). The access token is returned in the response header, and the refresh token is stored securely in an httpOnly cookie.

This operation is the primary authentication mechanism for member users to access their personal todo lists. The user is identified by email address, which serves as their unique identifier in the system.

Related operations: /auth/user/join for registration, /auth/user/refresh for token renewal.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for authenticating a user account.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and user identifier returned after successful login.

operations.specification: Service layer queries todo_app_users table for matching email. Uses bcrypt.compare to verify password_hash against submitted password. If validation passes, generates new JWT token pair with 15-minute access token and 7-day refresh token. Stores refresh token in secure persistent store. Returns access token in response header and refresh token in httpOnly cookie. Returns 401 if email not found or password invalid.

operations.name: refresh
operations.description:
Renews access tokens by validating and exchanging a valid refresh token for new access and refresh token pairs.

This operation accepts an existing refresh token (received during login or previous refresh) and validates its authenticity against the refresh token store. If valid, it generates a new JWT access token (valid for 15 minutes) and a new refresh token (valid for 7 days), invalidating the original refresh token in the process.

The implementation does not access the todo_app_users table directly but relies on the secure refresh token store. No user schema fields (email, password_hash, etc.) are involved in this refresh workflow.

The system maintains a refresh token blacklist for revoked tokens and enforces token expiration policies. This provides a secure way for users to maintain persistent sessions without requiring re-authentication with password credentials.

This operation is essential for maintaining user sessions without frequent re-authentication, providing both security and usability benefits.

Related operations: /auth/user/join for initial registration, /auth/user/login for initial authentication.

Returns access token in response header and new refresh token in httpOnly cookie.

Associates the guest with a temporary session in todo_app_guest_sessions with 60-minute expiration. Returns JWT access token valid for 15 minutes and refresh token valid for 7 days.

This operation creates a temporary guest account for unauthenticated users accessing the Todo App. The guest is identified by email and password, which are stored in the todo_app_guests table with the password_hash field. Upon successful registration, a session token is created in todo_app_guest_sessions with 60-minute expiration, allowing temporary access to the application. A JWT access token with 15-minute expiration and refresh token with 7-day expiration are issued. The operation validates that email is not already used by checking the todo_app_guests table, ensuring data integrity. This operation is public and accessible to any unauthenticated user.

This operation is required before any guest interaction with the system. It enables users to use guest features without a permanent account. The generated session and tokens expire according to system policy.

This operation triggers the registration workflow that sets up the guest's account state in the database and issues credentials for temporary access. It is the primary means of onboarding unauthenticated users.

For security, the password_hash field is always hashed before storage and never stored in plaintext. This ensures compliance with data protection standards.

This API is part of the guest authentication system, which provides limited access without requiring full registration or persistent identity.

Session records are updated in the todo_app_guest_sessions table with the new expiration timestamp. This operation fails if the refresh token has expired, is invalid, or does not correspond to an active guest session. Only temporary guest accounts can use this endpoint.

This endpoint supports temporary session maintenance for unauthenticated guest users. It provides a mechanism to remain active within the system without re-authenticating with credentials. This is essential for guest users who want to maintain session persistence within their limited access window.

The refresh operation is designed to minimize frequent re-authentication while maintaining security through short-lived access tokens and token rotation.

This operation is crucial for providing a seamless user experience for temporary guests who need to maintain access without full authentication.

All refresh tokens are stored securely and validated against the todo_app_guest_sessions table to prevent token reuse or hijacking.

operations.description:
Initiate email verification for a user account during the registration process. This operation validates a user's email address by confirming a unique verification token that was previously sent to the user's email address during account registration.

The system generates a one-time, time-limited token during user registration and stores it in the todo_app_user_email_verifications database table, linking it to the user's account. When a user clicks the verification link in their email, this endpoint receives the token as input and performs validation. If the token is valid, unexpired, and has not been previously used, the user's account status is updated to verified in the todo_app_users table and the verification record is removed for security.

This operation is critical for account security and ensuring email address legitimacy. Users who have not verified their email have limited functionality within the application. The verification token is designed to be single-use and expires after a defined period to prevent unauthorized access.

Security considerations include rate limiting to prevent brute force attacks on verification tokens and immediate deletion of used tokens to eliminate replay attack opportunities. This operation does not expose any personally identifiable information in its response, maintaining privacy standards.

operations.description:
Update a user's email verification status using a unique verification token.

This operation allows users to verify their email addresses by submitting a verification token that was sent to their email during registration. The system validates the token against the todo_app_user_email_verifications table, ensures it hasn't expired (typically 24-hour window), and confirms it hasn't been used previously. When valid, the operation updates the corresponding todo_app_users record to set the email_verified flag to true.

Security considerations include rate limiting on verification attempts, token expiration, and prevention of token reuse. The verification token must be a unique, cryptographically secure string that was previously generated and emailed to the user. This operation does not require authentication as the verification token serves as the authentication mechanism for this specific action.

This operation is the final step in the email verification workflow. After successful verification, the user's account transitions from unverified to verified status, enabling full access to all application features. Related operations: GET /auth/users/register (initiates verification), GET /auth/users/verify/email/resend (resends verification token).

Note: The todo_app_user_email_verifications table contains the tokens, their expiration timestamps, and usage status. The todo_app_users table contains the users' email addresses and verification status. This operation integrates both tables to complete the verification process.

This is a hard delete operation that completely removes the user record and all associated data from the database, including email verifications, password resets, sessions, and personal todo items. The account and its data are irreversibly purged from the system, which differs from soft delete operations.

This operation is available only to administrative actors with proper authorization. Normal users cannot delete their own accounts through this endpoint. Any attempt to delete an account that does not exist will return a 404 error.

The system does not maintain any historical records of deleted users for compliance or auditing purposes. All user data is purged permanently upon deletion. Related data such as todo items created by this user are also completely removed, as they cannot exist without a parent user account.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of todo items owned by the authenticated user.

This operation queries the todo_app_todo_items table and returns only items associated with the authenticated user's ID, ensuring complete data isolation between users. Users cannot view, filter, or access any todo items that do not belong to them. The operation supports advanced filtering by title (partial match), status, and creation date range, along with sorting by title, creation date, or completion status.

Security is enforced at both the API and database levels: the system extracts the user ID from the JWT authentication token and applies it as an implicit filter to all database queries. Any attempt to access another user's todo items via direct ID reference or manipulation of request parameters will result in a 404 Not Found response to prevent information disclosure. Title and description length constraints are validated at the API level, with the title restricted to 255 characters and the description restricted to 10,000 characters. Only valid status values ('pending', 'completed', 'archived') are allowed in search filters.

This operation is essential for the user's primary workflow of managing their personal todo list. It serves as the main interface for users to view, filter, and navigate their tasks. Related operations include creating a new todo item with POST /todos and updating or deleting an individual todo item with PUT /todos/{id} or DELETE /todos/{id}.

Validate request body fields against requirements: title must be string if provided, status must be one of 'pending', 'completed', 'archived'. Use user ID from JWT token as implicit WHERE clause condition. Return total count and cursor-based pagination tokens. Implement rate limiting at 10 requests per second per user. Include only id, title, status, createdAt fields in summary response for optimal performance.

Security is implemented at the service level through ownership validation. If the requested todo item doesn't exist or the authenticated user does not own it, the system returns a 404 Not Found response to prevent enumeration attacks. The returned data includes all fields of the todo item: content, completion status, creation timestamp, and update timestamp.

This operation supports the primary workflow of users viewing their individual todo items after they've been created or updated. It is a fundamental read operation that complements the creation, update, and deletion of todo items in the system. Related operations include PATCH /todos to list todos and PUT /todos/{todoItemId} to update a specific todo.

The created todo item is immediately accessible to the user who created it and is not visible to any other users. The system automatically sets the created_at timestamp to the current time. This operation does not support soft deletion; when a todo is deleted, it is permanently removed.

If the todo item does not exist or belongs to a different user, the operation returns a 404 Not Found error rather than 403 for security through obscurity.

The updated_at timestamp is automatically refreshed to reflect modification time. This operation must be atomic and transactional to ensure consistency. Related operations include retrieving a single todo item (GET /todos/{todoId}) and listing all user todos (GET /todos).

The database contains the todo_app_todo_items table with fields: id (UUID), title (string), content (text), completed (boolean), created_at (datetime), updated_at (datetime), and user_id (UUID). All updates are constrained to this structure.

The system prevents deletion of todo items belonging to other users through this access control.

Upon successful deletion, the full details of the deleted todo item are returned in the response body to allow the client to update its local state (e.g., remove the item from UI lists). When a user is authenticated, the update timestamp is extracted from the JWT token's 'updated_at' claim, which is updated during each successful authentication session refresh or profile update via the /users/{userId} PUT endpoint and stored in the authentication token payload.

id.description: Unique identifier for the user account. This is the primary key used to uniquely identify each user in the system.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_users.id column. UUID primary key generated by the database system.

ITodoAppUser.description: Complete user entity representing an authenticated user in the todo_app system. This object is returned when retrieving a user's profile information and contains all non-sensitive public fields. It identifies the user through their unique id and email address, includes their assigned username for display, and indicates whether their email has been verified. The timestamps track when the account was created and last modified. All sensitive information such as password hashes and authentication tokens are excluded for security reasons.
ITodoAppUser.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents the complete user entity with all public fields for the todo_app system. However, the underlying database table 'todo_app_users' contains only the 'id' column as a physical storage field. All other properties (email, username, email_verified, created_at, updated_at) are computed or derived based on system logic rather than direct database storage. This architecture separates identity (stored in database) from user representation (computed for API) to support potential future schema changes without API disruption. The system uses a combination of session storage, authentication tokens, and runtime computation to provide these fields. Authentication tokens (JWT) contain claims for all user properties, which are populated during login/registration and refreshed during session activity.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todo item. This is a system-generated UUID that uniquely identifies this specific todo item in the database.
id.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todo_items.id column. UUID primary key generated by the database system on record creation.

user.description: User who created this todo item. Contains essential user information for display without exposing the foreign key.
user.x-autobe-specification: Join via todo_app_todo_items.user_id to todo_app_users table. Returns ISummary variant with id, email, and username only. Prevents exposure of foreign key in response and enables client-side user context.

ITodoAppTodoItem.description: Complete representation of a todo item including all public fields from the database. This entity is returned when retrieving, updating, or deleting a specific todo item. It contains the content of the task, its completion status, and creation/update timestamps for tracking. The userId identifies the owner of this todo item within the application, but authentication is required to access this resource. This is the primary response model for todo item operations and represents the complete state of a todo task.
ITodoAppTodoItem.x-autobe-specification: This DTO represents the complete todo item entity with all public fields. The id and user_id fields are direct mappings from the todo_app_todo_items database table. The content, completed, createdAt, and updatedAt properties are not direct database columns but are computed: content from user input during creation, completed from user action, createdAt and updatedAt are system-generated timestamps that are not stored as separate columns in the database. All fields represent the complete state of a todo item. This schema is the primary representation of todo items in the API and is referenced by all todo item operations.

title.description: Partial title text to search for within todo items. Will match any todo item whose title contains the provided text (case-insensitive). Limited to 255 characters.
title.x-autobe-specification: Applies ILIKE '%title%' pattern to todo_app_todo_items.title field for partial text matching. Case-insensitive search across all user's todo items.

status.description: Filter todo items by their current status. Must be one of: 'pending', 'completed', or 'archived'. Allows users to view only tasks in a specific state.
status.x-autobe-specification: Filters todo_app_todo_items by exact status value ('pending', 'completed', 'archived'). Applied as explicit WHERE clause condition in database query.

createdAtStart.description: Minimum creation date for todo items (inclusive). Only return items created on or after this date and time in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).
createdAtStart.x-autobe-specification: Filters todo_app_todo_items by creation date - includes items created on or after this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format and applies >= condition to todo_app_todo_items.createdAt.

createdAtEnd.description: Maximum creation date for todo items (inclusive). Only return items created on or before this date and time in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ).
createdAtEnd.x-autobe-specification: Filters todo_app_todo_items by creation date - includes items created on or before this timestamp. Uses ISO 8601 format and applies <= condition to todo_app_todo_items.createdAt.

orderBy.description: Sort order for returned todo items. Options include: 'createdAt' (oldest first), 'createdAt:desc' (newest first), 'title' (A-Z), 'title:desc' (Z-A), 'status' (pending first), 'status:desc' (archived first).
orderBy.x-autobe-specification: Determines sorting order for results. Maps directly to SQL ORDER BY clauses: 'createdAt' (ASC), 'createdAt:desc' (DESC), 'title' (ASC), 'title:desc' (DESC), 'status' (ASC), 'status:desc' (DESC). Uses todo_app_todo_items.createdAt, todo_app_todo_items.title, and todo_app_todo_items.status fields.

limit.description: Maximum number of todo items to return in a single response. Must be between 1 and 100. Controls pagination size and prevents loading too many results at once.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Sets maximum number of todo items to return per page. Applied as LIMIT clause in SQL query with maximum value of 100 to prevent excessive resource usage.

ITodoAppTodoItem.IRequest.description: Search and pagination parameters for filtering todo items in the user's todo list. This object allows users to filter and sort their todo items by title (partial match), status, creation date range, and sorting preference. It controls pagination by limiting results per page. All parameters are optional and can be combined for complex queries, allowing users to efficiently navigate their todo items without fetching all records.
ITodoAppTodoItem.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request parameter type for API input, not a database entity. title: applies ILIKE '%title%' pattern to todo items title field. status: filters by exact status value ('pending', 'completed', 'archived'). createdAtStart/createdAtEnd: filters by date range using ISO 8601 format. orderBy: sorts results by 'createdAt', 'title', or 'status' in ascending or descending order. limit: sets maximum items per page with max value of 100. All parameters are optional and can be combined. This is a pure request type - no database persistence.
